text.p: - Slovenian government on Thursday decided to freeze the growth in salaries of the state's top officials and members of parliament until the year 1988.
- Minister of Economic Activities Marjan Senjur held talks with EU representatives concerning the standardisation of products in EU countries and associate EU members.
- Slovenian ministry of transport rejected accusations of protectionism from Croatia's gas monopoly INA.
- Primoz Peterka won the season's ninth ski-jumping event in Sweden's Falun on Thursday and thus extended his overall World Cup lead.
- Slovenia currently has 48 duty free shops mainly on its border crossings, which should be closed by July 1999 according to EU regulations.
- Slovenian Smelt Olimpija qualified for quarterfinals of the basketball Euroleague after beating Croatian Cibona by 62-61 on Thursday in Zagreb.
- Refinery Nafta Lendava is facing serious problems after Croatian INA decided to stop supplying Nafta with crude oil.
- Slovenian board for protection of environment will invest 16 billion tolars ($103.6 million) each year until 2010 for rationalisation of its handling of waste.
- Natural gas trader Geoplin said it sells gas cheaper than it is able to buy it. The company is constantly pushing for a 21 increase in prices of natural gas.
